title: Runtime fidelity sprint handbook: profiling, kernel interactions, and rollback protocols
author: Maya Chen
content:
Overview

This handbook describes the goals, lab protocol, measurement artifacts, and safe rollback procedures for a 'fidelity sprint' — a focused engineering sprint whose objective is to change or validate runtime fidelity (model variant, quantization, kernel variant, batching policy, or routing policy) without regressing customer-facing SLOs or quality metrics. It is intended for engineers, SREs, and applied ML practitioners who run experiments across the serving runtime.

Why a fidelity sprint?
- Reduce regressions: small behavioral changes in kernels, quantization, or batching can introduce subtle regressions in output quality or latency distribution.
- Reproducibility: define a repeatable lab protocol for new kernel rollouts and quantization profiles.
- Operational safety: codify rollback and guardrails that preserve availability and cost targets.

Scope
- Applies to changes that affect inference fidelity or execution internals: kernel variants, quantized weights/ops, KV-cache prefetch hints, scheduler admission policies, batching heuristics, and model-variant routing.
- Does NOT cover: API surface changes, control-plane-only feature flips, or customer-facing configuration changes that don't change execution fidelity.

Owners and stakeholders
- Sprint lead: owner of the change (name + pager) — typically a runtime or applied-ML engineer.
- QA / Evals: applied-ml team responsible for the prompt-suite and regression gates.
- Oncall SRE: responsible for rollout monitoring and rapid rollback steps.
- Product owner: for business risk decisions when rolling out to Dedicated/Private customers.

SLOs and acceptance criteria
- Latency SLOs: 99th percentile tail latency increase <= 10% relative to baseline for the same workload mix.
- Error budget: no more than 5% additional errors (5xx or runtime timeouts) during canary windows.
- Quality gate: prompt-eval pass-rate delta <= 0.5% absolute (for high-sensitivity tasks) or <= 2% for low-sensitivity tasks.
- Cost delta: per-token cost increase <= 5% (unless explicitly approved).

Labs and environment matrix (table)
- The lab matrix documents target hardware, kernel variants, and fidelity settings we exercise:

| Environment | GPU type | Kernel variant | Model variant | Typical sequence lengths | Notes |
|-------------|----------|----------------|---------------|-------------------------|-------|
| local-lab-rt | A100 80GB | v2-lowlat | fp16 | 32-128 | dev-only, limited concurrency |
| perf-lab-1 | A100S | v2-default | int8-q | 16-256 | synthetic replay of production traces |
| canary-region | T4/GPU | v2-explicit-prefetch | fp16 | 8-512 | small % of real traffic |
| dedicated-staging | H100 | v3-kernel-tiling | int8-q | 64-1024 | reserved for enterprise smoke tests |

Prerequisites (checklist)
1) Baseline capture: collect a 24-hour production trace and compute baseline SLOs and per-route token distribution.
2) Eval prompt set: ensure there is a labeled prompt set for at least three sensitivity tiers (high/medium/low).
3) Telemetry hooks: feature flags, kernel parameter tags, and tracing for kernel decisions must be enabled.
4) Canary plan: percentage targets, ramp schedule, and alert thresholds declared in the sprint ticket.

Experiment procedure (numbered steps)
1. Prepare artifacts\   a. Build the kernel/quantization artifact and tag with semver: kernel:vX.Y.Z-fidelity-sprint\   b. Generate a benchmark spec (JSON) that includes: route list, concurrency shape, sequence-length distribution, and sample prompt corpus. Example: {"routes": ["chat_v1","completion_short"], "concurrency": "Poisson(8)", "sample_corpus": "gs://redwood-evals/fidelity-sprint/"}
2. Run lab smoke tests (local-lab-rt)\   a. Execute unit-level smoke with trace replay: ./scripts/replay_trace.sh --trace=24h-baseline --kernel=kernel:vX.Y.Z\   b. Validate memory, no OOMs, and kernel logs for warnings.
3. Microbenchmark suite (perf-lab-1)\   a. Run throughput and tail-latency suite: python tools/bench_runner.py --spec fidelity_bench.json --out /tmp/bench-results.json\   b. Record: p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, GPU UTIL, kernel occupancy.
4. Offline quality evals\   a. Run the labeled prompt-set through both baseline and candidate artifacts: eval-runner --baseline s3://... --candidate s3://... --metrics rouge,bert-score,exact_match\   b. Produce a delta report and flag prompts with >X% change for manual review.
5. Canary rollout\   a. Start with 0.5% traffic in canary-region for 30 minutes. Monitor SLO and eval signal.\   b. If green, ramp to 2% for 2 hours, then to 10% for 4 hours.\   c. During each window, run shadow-mirroring to capture full outputs for offline eval.
6. Production ramp and final validation\   a. Only after meeting acceptance criteria for two independent canary windows do we proceed to full region or Dedicated rollout.\\n
Monitoring and telemetry (what to watch)
- Latency heatmap per route and per-sequence-length bin.
- Kernel decision rate: % of requests using new kernel vs fallback.
- Error types: kernel-timeout, OOM, scheduler-rejected, model-internal-errors.
- Output divergence fingerprints: fingerprint ID match rate between baseline and candidate outputs (approximate hash equality).
- Cost signals: per-route GPU time, kernel time breakdown, and billing samples.

Alert thresholds (sample)
- p99 latency increase > 12% for >5m -> page_oncall (P1)\- error-rate increase > 5% for >5m -> page_oncall (P1)\- eval-pass-rate drop > 1% absolute for high-sensitivity prompts (manual review) -> escalate to product + applied-ml

Rollback procedure (runbook)
1) Automated rollback trigger \   - If any P1 alert above fires during canary, the system must automatically flip routing to baseline kernel variant for the affected cohort.
2) Manual rollback steps (if automation unavailable)\   a. Oncall runs: curl -XPOST https://controlplane.internal/api/rollout/rollback -d '{"target":"kernel:vX.Y.Z","reason":"p99-latency"}'\   b. Confirm traffic reverts using: k get routes --selector fidelity-sprint=true -o wide\   c. Validate telemetry: confirm p99 returns to baseline within 3x of mean reversion time (typically 2 minutes).
3) Post-rollback actions\   a. Create a hotfix ticket, attach all trace artifacts and eval failure cases.\   b. Hold a 2-hour warroom with applied-ml and kernel-owner to triage.\\n
Quality analysis guidelines
- For each flagged prompt, capture: input, baseline output, candidate output, token-level alignments, and logits (where available).
- Use the scoring rubric: 1=identical, 2=minor wording difference (acceptable), 3=meaningful semantic change (requires escalation), 4=hallucination/regression (blocker).
- Tag each prompt with sensitivity and business impact.

Kernel scheduling interplay notes (short guide)
- Batching tradeoffs: larger batches improve throughput but increase latency tail for short-sequence requests. During fidelity sprints focus on sequence-length-aware batching (max_batch_size per-seqlen-bin).\- Preemption: enable preemption for priority traffic to avoid head-of-line latency for interactive routes. Validate preemption counters don't inflate kernel switch rate by >3x.\- KV-cache prefetching: for long chat sessions, prefetching reduces token latency but increases memory pressure. Add memory headroom checks and a soft cap of 80% GPU memory for prefetch cache.

Benchmarks and artifact naming convention
- Bench artifact names: fidelity-bench.{kernel_tag}.{model_tag}.{gpu}.{date}.json\- Always store raw traces, aggregated metrics, and the prompt-evaluation delta report in: gs://redwood-bench/fidelity-sprints/{sprint_id}/

Reporting and post-mortem
- After the sprint complete (success or rollback), the sprint lead must produce a 1-page summary with: baseline vs candidate summary table, failure cases, root cause hypothesis, and recommended next steps. Attach raw artifacts and the canary ramp timeline.

Appendices
A) Example benchmark spec (JSON)\\{
  "sprint_id": "fs-2026-07-23",
  "routes": ["chat_v1"],
  "shapes": [{"concurrency":10, "seq_len":64}],
  "duration_minutes": 60
}\\n
B) Quick commands\- Collect runtime traces: ./tools/capture_runtime_trace --duration 60 --out /tmp/trace.json\- Run bench: python tools/bench_runner.py --spec /tmp/fidelity_bench.json --kernel kernel:vX.Y.Z --out /tmp/results.json\- Trigger rollback (manual): ./scripts/rollback_kernel.sh --target kernel:baseline

C) FAQ\- Q: Can we skip shadow-mirroring during canary?\   A: No — shadow outputs are the primary artifact for post-rollout quality analysis.\- Q: Who signs off a Dedicated customer rollout?\   A: Product + Customer Success + Security (if private deployment).

Document maintenance
- Owner: Maya Chen (runtime). Update cadence: before every major kernel release or every 6 months.
- Record of changes: last major revision consolidated monitoring thresholds (2026-11-30).
